payload.body: dc: usage-rules.md is drafted for your review: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-matts-Devel-prj-Pplr/da774a51-7916-4f68-b76b-37c788cb4a76/scratchpad/docs/usage-rules.md, with the diff at /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-matts-Devel-prj-Pplr/da774a51-7916-4f68-b76b-37c788cb4a76/scratchpad/docs/usage-rules.diff. The CHANGELOG's Fixed gains the line on pplr tags' usage (vc decision 14), re-banked on dc/wp13-docs at ff15b57. usage-rules.md is a rewrite, because every section was the legacy's. Core principles: one folder per person; the two ways to name a person and which commands take which; the template's file names; pplr writes what it generates; dry runs first (the --apply and --dry-run commands named); and _pplr/ for pplr's own files. People: new, about, edit, open -t, rename and pictures, with DOs for new's URL, rename over a hand move, and the About header's fields. Tags, the centre: tags.yaml per person; hand tags as bare words, never rewritten; auto and inferred tags from a reviewed list through tags apply, an inferred tag being a relationship tag; one word of lowercase letters and digits, in the vocabulary, which gives the facet and folds old words through also and split; cadence tags; tag show and edit, tags check and render; never edit the Tags line, _tags/ or tags_index.json. Contact cadence: contact.yaml's fields; roster:, every: and the person's own cadence:, in that order of strength; a booked meeting; scan, due, log, next, then email and log --email N; never edit the (Contact).md view. Contacts: check first, every other mode a dry run until --apply, the .vcf backup first, plan then apply-plan (read by headers), nothing removed in either direction, and the JSON dump off macOS. Searching and indexes: search, grep and grep -t, meetings, reindex and doctor --fix. Then a table of the generated files and what writes each, the anti-patterns, and the integration notes. Each claim is checked against src at c4929d0, including the tag word rule (tags.rs, lowercase letters and digits only, so the old 'machine-learning' example would fail check), open's flags before the names, and render rebuilding tags_index.json. Prettier passes, and there is no non-ASCII. Like the CHANGELOG, it describes the Rust binary, so tell me whether it lands now or after C5. Nothing in it is untrue of main today. The README is next.
